transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Cora Vakulman.
Stocks opened higher this morning as the Commerce Department reported the U.S. trade deficit
widened in August.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones industrial average rose about 350 points in
early trading.
The nation's trade gap widened nearly 14 percent in August to just under $106 billion.
Exports and imports both rose during the month, but imports rose faster.
President Trump has tried to narrow the trade deficit by imposing double-digit taxes on
imported goods, but imports continue to climb.
Imports from China were higher in August than they were a year ago.
Oil prices have been slower, with the international benchmark dropping below $100 a barrel.
Oil gasoline and diesel prices showed little change overnight.
And the $81 billion merger, the Skydance Paramount and Warner Brothers Discovery, is now official.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
Germany's former foreign intelligence agency chief has been arrested on suspicion of treasonous
espionage.
A former high-ranking agency aide has also been arrested.
As Esme Nicholson reports from Berlin, prosecutors have not yet commented on whether the men
were spying for a foreign actor.
Germany's federal prosecutor's office says Auguste Haning will be brought before a federal
judge on charges that include treasonous espionage and attempted treason.
Haning, now 80, served as the head of Germany's foreign intelligence agency known as the BND
between 1998 and 2005.
Officers have also arrested a current intelligence officer named only as Manfred D. for allegedly
aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage.
The aide is suspected of providing the intelligence agency's former chief with thousands of classified
documents in exchange for money.
Haning then allegedly used this information for his private consultancy work.
For NPR News, I'm Esme Nicholson, in Berlin.
Israel's defense minister says its military is on high alert ahead of the three-year anniversary
of the October 7th Hamas-led attack.
That says a ceasefire has been declared in Gaza for nearly a year, despite ongoing Israeli
strikes, as NPR's Cat Lonsdorf reports.
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz put out a warning ahead of the October 7th anniversary,
saying that Israeli intelligence indicated that Hamas is planning to carry out attacks
against Israeli forces in Gaza.
He said that if such attacks occur, "Hamas and the population of Gaza will pay a heavy
price beyond proportion."
The statement comes just a day after Katz claimed Israel still intends to "eliminate"
2,000 members of Hamas who carried out the October 7th assault.
It's been nearly a year since a ceasefire was declared in Gaza, which has still seen
near-daily deadly Israeli strikes on Palestinians.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to continue targeting anyone involved
in the 2023 attack.
Cat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Both Pakistan and Turkey say they will send troops to Saudi Arabia.
It's part of their new defense pact.
Iran announced the news yesterday, saying a retired Pakistani military officer would
lead the effort.
It's not yet clear how many troops will be deployed.
This comes as Saudi-backed forces in neighboring Yemen battle Houthi rebels.
Both sides have claimed attacks on each other.
An American citizen who was shot and wounded by Border Patrol agents in Chicago is now
suing the government.
Madre Mar Martinez, a teacher's assistant, was shot several times.
She alleges the shooting was not justified and the agents were never in danger.
The agents first claimed she used her vehicle to hit them, but the charges against her were
later dropped.
Televangelist Jim Baker has died, and NPR's Jason Derose reports he was 86 years old.
Jim Baker began working at the Christian Broadcasting Network in the late 1960s, eventually hosting
the evangelical talk show The 700 Club.
In the early 1970s, he and his wife Tammy Faye Baker helped create the Trinity Broadcasting
Network and a show of their own called the PTL Club.
PTL stood for Praise the Lord.
"Greater is he that is in you right, in me, than he that's in the world.
The sun will shine again."
In 1987, two scandals, one involving sexual misconduct and one involving financial fraud,
brought down Baker's ministry.
By 2007, he'd returned to the airwaves, hosting The Jim Baker Show from Branson, Missouri.
Jason Derose, NPR News.
And I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News, from Washington.
This election season, you can streamline your news intake with Up First.
Our team of reporters and editors works overnight, so you can start every morning with three
stories you need to know.
And short episodes, 12-14 minutes long, to save you time and your sanity.
Follow Up First on the NPR app or wherever you get your podcasts.

Dow Jones industrial average rose about 350 points in early trading
International oil benchmark dropped below $100 a barrel
Skydance and Paramount and Warner Brothers Discovery merger valued at $81 billion now official
Germany's former foreign intelligence chief Auguste Haning arrested on suspicion of treasonous espionage
Current German intelligence officer Manfred D. arrested for aiding treasonous espionage
Israel's defense minister warns of high alert ahead of October 7th Hamas attack anniversary
Pakistan and Turkey say they will send troops to Saudi Arabia as part of defense pact
